adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the approved 1962 Benziger printing sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Ordo Missae of Pallottinum, Poznań 1963, which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
The approved Benziger printing's punctuation is retained. The difference marks phrasing and does not change the words.
The approved Benziger printing's capitalization is retained. The pinned digital reading is recorded exactly; the word is the same.

The separately excerpted middle formula on p. 123 stops with Deus. The selected continuous conclusion retains the comma attested in the pinned digital reading and in Rubricae generales 115 a; it is not silently attributed to that printed page.

The terminal chant formula on p. 226 begins with uppercase Per. The selected continuous conclusion retains lowercase per, as in the pinned digital reading and Rubricae generales 115 a; the separate printed start is recorded without inventing a continuous source.
